---
title: "Releases, the data dictionary and warnings"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

Most of the warnings a new sRtr user sees come from one question: which
version of the SRTR data dictionary describes my files? This article
answers it, explains each warning `load_srtr_file()` gives, and shows how a
script can count warnings instead of hiding them.

The examples use sRtr's stored dictionaries and one tiny made-up file, so
they run on this site.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(sRtr)
```

# Releases

SRTR delivers standard analysis files (SAFs) in releases named by year and
month: `"2303"` is the March 2023 release. Variables are added and dropped
between releases, so the dictionary that labels your files should be the
one for your release.

sRtr stores copies of SRTR's public data dictionary page, one per version
it has seen:

```{r snapshots}
dictionary_versions$releases[, c("snapshot", "release", "retrieved")]
```

For a release that has a stored copy, sRtr uses that copy. For a release
between two copies, it uses what the two have in common:

```{r interpolated}
d2303 <- srtr_dictionary("2303")
attr(d2303, "basis")
```

# What a release between two copies can and cannot know

Between the stored 2203 and 2609 copies, no variable's label, type or
format changed, and no format code changed meaning. The differences are
variables that appear in only one copy:

```{r differences}
key <- function(d) paste(d$Dataset, d$Variable)
d2203 <- srtr_dictionary("2203")
d2609 <- srtr_dictionary("2609")

c(
  only_in_2203 = length(setdiff(key(d2203), key(d2609))),
  only_in_2609 = length(setdiff(key(d2609), key(d2203))),
  in_both = length(intersect(key(d2203), key(d2609)))
)
head(setdiff(key(d2203), key(d2609)), 3)
head(setdiff(key(d2609), key(d2203)), 3)
```

For example, the waitlist files list `CAN_LISTING_CTR_ID` in 2203 and
`CAN_LISTING_CTR_CD` with `CAN_LISTING_CTR_TY` in 2609. Whether a 2303
file has the old column, the new ones or both cannot be known from the two
copies, so the 2303 dictionary leaves all of them out:

```{r left-out}
nrow(d2303) == length(intersect(key(d2203), key(d2609)))
```

`load_srtr_file()` does not lose those columns: it reads them from your
file and labels them from whichever copy lists them.

Two more points about the stored copies:

- A copy's date is when SRTR published that page or sRtr retrieved it, not
  when a variable was first collected. A variable that first appears in the
  2609 copy may have been collected long before. To find when a variable is
  actually filled in, look at the data (see
  [Missing data](missing-data.html)).
- If a later copy changes a variable between two copies, a release in
  between gets the earlier definition, with a warning. `gaps = "error"`
  stops instead, and `gaps = "nearest"` stays silent. With the two copies
  sRtr has now, this does not happen.

A release before the first copy or after the last uses the nearest one,
with a warning:

```{r outside}
early <- srtr_dictionary("2101")
attr(early, "snapshot")
```

# Telling sRtr your release

sRtr takes the release from, in order:

1. the `release` argument of `load_srtr_file()`;
2. `set_srtr_wd(release = )`;
3. a folder named `pubsafYYMM`, such as `pubsaf2303`;
4. otherwise, the bundled dictionary (`sRtr::dictionary`).

Every loaded file records which it used. Here is a tiny made-up waitlist
file in a folder named for release 2303.

On your own files you would call `set_srtr_wd()`. That changes the folder
and release for the whole R session, so the example instead points sRtr at
the made-up folder only while each call runs, with `in_example()`. Your own
folder and release are untouched if you run it.

```{r make-file}
dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "pubsaf2303")
dir.create(dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
cand <- data.frame(
  PX_ID = 1:4,
  CAN_LISTING_CTR_ID = c(11, 11, 12, 13),
  CAN_ABO = c("A", "O", "UNK", "B"),
  CAN_LISTING_DT = as.Date("2021-01-01") + 0:3
)
suppressWarnings(haven::write_sas(cand, file.path(dir, "cand_kipa.sas7bdat")))

# Instead of set_srtr_wd(dir), for this example only.
in_example <- function(expr) withr::with_envvar(c(SRTR_WD = dir), expr)
```

```{r load}
cand_kipa <- in_example(load_srtr_file("CAND_KIPA"))
```

The two warnings are the subject of the next sections. First, what was
recorded:

```{r recorded}
str(attr(cand_kipa, "srtr_release"))
```

`release` came from the folder name (`basis`), and `dictionary` says it
was filled in between two copies. To repeat your labels, someone needs all
of this attribute and the same version of sRtr, because a later version
can store another copy of the dictionary or change a correction. Save the
attribute with your results, and record the sRtr version you used:

```{r version, eval = FALSE}
packageVersion("sRtr")
# Installed from GitHub: the commit, if recorded
packageDescription("sRtr")$RemoteSha
```

A lockfile (for example from renv) pins the version for you.

`CAN_LISTING_CTR_ID` kept its label even though the 2303 dictionary left it
out:

```{r kept-label}
attr(cand_kipa$CAN_LISTING_CTR_ID, "label")
```

# Missing columns

The first warning lists the dictionary's columns that the file lacks.
This made-up file has only four columns. On real files, the usual causes
are a dictionary for the wrong release, or an extract SRTR delivered with
fewer columns. Check the release first. `column_check = "error"` turns the
warning into an error, and `column_check = "none"` turns it off.

The check runs only when you read every column. With `col_select`, sRtr
reads the columns you name (a name the file lacks is an error) and does not
compare the file with the dictionary, so no warning there says nothing
about the columns you did not select.

# Codes in no format

The second warning is about values that no SRTR format lists, here
`"UNK"` in `CAN_ABO`. Their meaning is not documented, so sRtr keeps them
as their own factor level and names them as such:

```{r not-in-format}
table(cand_kipa$CAN_ABO)
```

sRtr warns every time, rather than recoding them, because only a source
document can say what they mean. Decide for your analysis, and say what you
decided. [Checking sRtr on your own SAFs](checking-your-safs.html) shows how
to count these values on your files.

# Corrections to SRTR's dictionary

sRtr corrects a few entries of SRTR's web dictionary that do not match the
files. Each has an ID, and every load records which were applied (the
`corrections` field above). The one correction so far gives `REC_COD`, the
recipient cause of death, the format `COD` instead of the thoracic `THCOD`:

```{r corrections}
web <- srtr_dictionary("2609", view = "web")
corrected <- srtr_dictionary("2609")
c(
  web = unique(web$FormatID[web$Variable == "REC_COD"]),
  corrected = unique(corrected$FormatID[corrected$Variable == "REC_COD"])
)
```

`view = "web"`, in `srtr_dictionary()` or `load_srtr_file()`, gives the
dictionary as SRTR's pages have it, without corrections. For a release
between two stored copies, it is still filled in from the copies on either
side; before the first or after the last, it uses the nearest copy, with a
warning. The
[`srtr_dictionary()` help page](../reference/srtr_dictionary.html) lists
every correction and its evidence.

# Counting warnings instead of hiding them

`suppressWarnings()` hides every warning, including ones you have not seen
before. Every sRtr warning has a class, so a script can collect each kind
and decide what to do with it:

```{r collect}
seen <- list()
collect <- function(expr) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    expr,
    sRtr_warning = function(w) {
      kind <- class(w)[1]
      seen[[kind]] <<- c(seen[[kind]], conditionMessage(w))
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  )
}

cand_kipa <- collect(in_example(load_srtr_file("CAND_KIPA")))
lengths(seen)
```

Warnings from other packages still reach you. Read `seen` yourself; on
real files the messages can contain values from your data, so do not
share them as they are (see
[Share counts only](checking-your-safs.html#share-counts-only)).

To silence one kind you have already looked at, and only that kind:

```{r one-kind}
quiet_codes <- function(expr) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    expr,
    sRtr_warning_unknown_codes = function(w) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  )
}
cand_kipa <- quiet_codes(in_example(load_srtr_file("CAND_KIPA")))
```

The codes warning is gone; the missing-columns warning still shows.

# Checklist

- Know your release, and give it to `set_srtr_wd()` or name the folder
  `pubsafYYMM`.
- Save `attr(x, "srtr_release")` and the sRtr version with your analysis.
- Read each missing-columns warning once; check the release if you did not
  expect it.
- Decide what each code in no format means for your analysis.
- Collect warnings by class rather than suppressing them all.
